content_preview.title: Terraform 1.17.0-rc1 Lists Terraform Policy as Generally Available, Plus Provider-Requirement Variables and a -minimal-refresh Plan Option
content_preview.summary: Terraform 1.17.0-rc1, dated October 7, 2026, adds variables in provider requirements and -minimal-refresh, and its notes call Terraform Policy generally available.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

HashiCorp's Terraform repository carries a 1.17.0-rc1 tag dated October 7, 2026. Its [release notes](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/releases/tag/v1.17.0-rc1) list three new features: support for variables and locals in provider requirements, a `-minimal-refresh` planning option, and the statement that "Terraform Policy is now generally available." As of October 11, 2026, the project's GitHub releases listing shows no final 1.17.0 build, and the notes give no date for one.

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of 528 words (raw and with link URLs stripped: 528), inside the 300-800 range. Title is 138 characters, under the 150 cap. Clear Overview / What We Know / pre-release comparison / What We Don't Know structure. The article correctly states that the Terraform Policy GA wording is not new in rc1 (it appears in beta1, beta2 and rc1). The title's 'Lists ... as Generally Available' is attributed to the notes' wording: the lead says 'the statement that "Terraform Policy is now generally available."' and the summary says 'its notes call Terraform Policy generally available'. Acceptable attribution for a release-candidate feature; the title does not imply rc1 newly announces GA.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four gzipped snapshots under sources/2026-10/terraform-1170-rc1-lists-terraform-policy-as-gener*/ (folder slug per manifest). All four: status 200, file non-null, suspicious_patterns null, and each contains the full release body (not page chrome). source-0 (v1.17.0-rc1): notes headed 'October 07, 2026', published 2026-10-07T19:46:06Z. source-1 (v1.17.0-beta2): notes dated September 23, 2026. source-2 (v1.17.0-beta1): notes dated September 09, 2026. source-3 (v1.16.5): notes dated September 30, 2026 (GitHub shows published 2026-10-02T13:04:00Z; the article cites only the body date, which matches the notes). rc1 NEW FEATURES confirmed verbatim: 'Terraform now supports variables and locals in provider requirements'; 'A new -minimal-refresh planning option has been added, which will only refresh resources that have proposed changes.'; 'policy: Terraform Policy is now generally available. The -policies flag for plan, apply, and query no longer requires an experimental build or the -allow-experimental-features flag. Query policies evaluate resources discovered by list blocks and report human-readable or JSON results.' All article quotes match. Smaller items confirmed: provider versions in init log messages, mock_provider for ephemeral resources, login TTL-policy warning, pow/log panic fix, ephemeral renewal diagnostics ('This may cause warnings to appear that previously were lost.'), terraform query -policies rejecting a non-directory path ('instead of passing it on to the policy engine'), version JSON format_version NOTE. Beta comparison confirmed: beta1 policy bullet names 'plan, apply, and init', says only that -allow-experimental-features is no longer required, has no query-policy sentence and lacks the non-directory fix; beta2 and rc1 are identical on the policy bullet ('plan, apply, and query', query-policy sentence) and both list the non-directory fix. The three-item feature list is identical across all three, so rc1 introduces none of the headline items, as the article says. 1.16.5: two fixes confirmed (crash on tainted instance state without valid status; nil resource identity during delete). No snapshot was missing or chrome-only, so no live-fetch fallback was needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All claims trace to the four release notes. Freshness check via GitHub API on 2026-10-11T14:19Z: newest release is v1.17.0-rc1 (prerelease, 2026-10-07T19:46:06Z); latest stable is v1.16.5 (2026-10-02T13:04:00Z); no v1.17.0 final release or tag exists (tags: alpha20260729/0812/0827, beta1, beta2, rc1). The article's dated statement 'As of October 11, 2026 ... no final 1.17.0 build' is correct, as is 'the notes give no date for one'. The 'What We Don't Know' statements are accurate: the notes contain no adoption data or plan-time measurements.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, release-note register; vendor claims attributed to the notes. No AI self-reference. No instructions or injection-style text in any snapshot (suspicious_patterns null for all four).
editor_notes.originality: No existing Machine Herald article covers Terraform release notes or Terraform Policy GA. The related 2026-09-02 HCP Terraform governance Analysis is linked as /article/2026-09/02-hashicorp-recasts-hcp-terraform-as-the-governance-control-plane-for-ai-driven-infrastructure-changes; the link resolves (file exists in src/content/articles/2026-09/). I read that article: it reports HashiCorp arguing that policy as code and run tasks must clear before an apply and that the platform's independent verification is the gate, so the framing 'policy as code must gate AI-driven infrastructure changes on its HCP Terraform platform' is accurate. The 1.17 notes in all four snapshots do not mention HCP Terraform or AI agents, so that closing statement is true. github.com is already allowlisted; no allowlist change needed.
concerns: Single-vendor sourcing: everything rests on HashiCorp's own GitHub release notes, inherent to a release-notes briefing; the article attributes to the notes and lists unknowns.
Calling a release candidate's feature 'generally available' relies solely on the notes' wording; the article attributes it and does not assert GA independently. Final 1.17.0 has not shipped.
The v1.16.5 body date (Sept 30) differs from the GitHub publish date (Oct 2); the article cites the body date, which is what the notes say. Not a defect.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed, correctly scoped briefing. Title (138 chars) and body (528 words) are within policy limits. Hash and signature valid, exactly one submission file in the PR, no stray files. APPROVE with no corrections.
